findings.claim: the doctor's derived battery check scans only top-level tools/*.mjs, so nested battery members (tools/bench/grade.mjs, tools/zcode-plugin/lib/gate-law.mjs) are invisible to it — removing either from package.json's selftest would pass the doctor, the exact silent-skip class issue #16 closed
findings.proof: delete 'node tools/zcode-plugin/lib/gate-law.mjs --self-test' from the battery script: doctor still passes (nested file never listed), battery loses the plugin's law coverage silently
findings.dedupKey: tools/task-coverage.mjs cmddoctor readdirsync(tools) non-recursive vs package.json selftest with 8 members

findings.claim: the banner's additionalContext JSON shape cannot be validated outside the client; fail-open means a runner schema drift silently no-ops the banner while the gate keeps working
findings.evidence: tools/zcode-plugin/hooks/banner.mjs catch-and-exit-0; the strict hook-output schema is documented but not machine-checkable here
findings.dedupKey: tools/zcode-plugin/hooks/banner.mjs catch-and-exit-0; the strict hook-output schema is documented but not machine-checkable here
findings.justification: the banner is advisory context by design and fails open; its JSON shape can only be validated by the client runner that consumes it — the README registers the boundary and the gate's exit-code channel is unaffected

findings.claim: the gate trusts the runner-supplied cwd as its walk-up start — a lying payload could point at a different harness repo and borrow ITS tasks
findings.justification: the hook payload is the runner's own trust boundary; the staged gate and push fence re-judge every edit against the repo's own ROOT at commit and push time, so a lying cwd buys nothing that survives the next transport
